rationale: PINS the one rule protobuf's resolution fixtures cannot otherwise see, and pins it in BOTH directions so it cannot be satisfied by a rule that merely prefers the closest declaration. A type written inside an `extend` block is resolved from where the block is WRITTEN, because `extend` opens no scope: the extended type is where the block's members go, not a scope their types are looked up in. The analyzer carried one value for both questions (`Ctx.owner`), so a reference inside a NESTED `extend` was resolved against a type the language never made a scope of. ROW 1 (`leaf_ref`) is the shape the reference implementation's own `unittest_custom_options.proto` uses: the block is nested inside `Nest.Leaf` and writes the name `Leaf`, so C++ lookup walks out from `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf` to the declaration `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf`. Pre-fix the analyzer emitted `nse.demo.Leaf`, an id published by no file in any repository. ROW 2 (`which_twin`) is the guard: the block is at FILE SCOPE and two types are named `Twin`, so a rule that always preferred the innermost declaration would answer `nse.demo.Dual.Twin` and be wrong. protoc answers `nse.demo.Twin`. ROW 3 (`shadow`) is the control: an ordinary field in the same message, resolving to the nested type, so a fix that broke in-file resolution for nested types would fail it. OWNERSHIP is asserted on both extension members, because a one-sided fix that moved the resolution scope by also moving ownership would produce two correct edges and one wrong `contains`. BOTH ROWS ARE ADJUDICATED BY THE REFERENCE COMPILER, not only by this lane: `protoc` 36.2 on this exact file reports `leaf_ref -> .nse.demo.Nest.Leaf` and `which_twin -> .nse.demo.Twin`, which are the two `uses` targets asserted below.

expectRelationships.note: THE row this fixture exists for. `Leaf` is written inside an `extend` block nested in `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf`, so it resolves from THAT scope: the candidate `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf.Leaf` does not exist, the walk steps out one scope and `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf` does, and that is the declaration. The pre-fix answer was `nse.demo.Leaf` — the package plus the name as written — because the walk had been handed `google.protobuf.FieldOptions`, every candidate derived from it fell outside the package subtree and was dropped, and nothing inside the subtree is named `Leaf`. `nse.demo.Leaf` is published by no file in any repository in the corpus. protoc 36.2, run on this fixture, reports this field's type as `.nse.demo.Nest.Leaf`.

The `extend` block is written INSIDE `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf`, so the extension's own name is `nse.demo.Nest.Leaf.leaf_ref` while the extendee `google.protobuf.FieldOptions` names the edge's SOURCE. `protoc` reads this member's extension name as `.nse.demo.Nest.Leaf.leaf_ref` with `extendee = .google.protobuf.FieldOptions` — read back from the descriptor set of this fixture, so the two fields are separately visible rather than inferred.

THE guard row, and the reason this fixture is two rows. The `extend Dual` block is at FILE SCOPE and two declarations are named `Twin`: `nse.demo.Twin` and `nse.demo.Dual.Twin`. C++ lookup from the file-scope scope `nse.demo` finds `nse.demo.Twin` and stops; `nse.demo.Dual` is not an enclosing scope of a file-scope extend block. Pre-fix the walk was handed `nse.demo.Dual` and answered `nse.demo.Dual.Twin`. A rule stated as 'always prefer the innermost declaration' passes ROW 1 and fails this row, which is what makes this a rule about where the block is written rather than a rule about proximity. This is `unittest_delimited.proto`'s construction: it declares `editions_unittest.LengthPrefixed` at file scope and `editions_unittest.TestDelimited.LengthPrefixed` nested, then writes `LengthPrefixed lengthprefixed = 1004;` inside a file-scope `extend TestDelimited`. protoc answers `editions_unittest.LengthPrefixed`. The SOURCE of this edge is the extension itself, and pass 21 corrected its id: the `extend Dual` block is at file scope, so `protoc` names the extension `nse.demo.which_twin` with `extendee = .nse.demo.Dual`. The resolution TARGET is unchanged by that fix and is still `nse.demo.Twin` — which is the point of the row, since `nse.demo.Dual.which_twin` was a name `protoc` does not define.

The control. An ordinary field of `Dual` writing `Twin` resolves to the nested `nse.demo.Dual.Twin`, not the file-scope `nse.demo.Twin`, because the enclosing scope `nse.demo.Dual` has the nearer declaration. Present so a change that pushed in-file resolution outward through the package for every reference would fail here, and so ROW 2's answer cannot be read as 'always prefer the outermost' either.

forbidRelationships.note: The pre-fix answer, forbidden explicitly. A forbidden row rather than only an absent requirement, so a regression that emitted BOTH the right and the wrong target fails instead of passing on the right one alone.
The pre-fix answer for the guard row, and the answer 'prefer the innermost declaration' gives. Forbidden so that rule cannot pass this fixture.
THE pass-21 pre-fix extension id, forbidden explicitly. `protoc` reads this member's extension name as `nse.demo.which_twin`; `Dual` is the extendee and appears only as the edge's source.
THE pass-21 pre-fix id for the same reason at a different nesting depth: the block is written inside `Nest.Leaf`, so the name follows the block, not the extendee.
